newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yen bond rally not in line with economy - officials.
newsitem.headline: Yen bond rally not in line with economy - officials.

text.p: Recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy, in which production has begun to show some strength, senior government officials said on Wednesday.
One official said auto production, in particular, has been accelerating amid an overall recovery in industrial production.

"Looking at yen bond futures, the upward trend is still in place, though the excessive rally has somewhat subsided. There is a clear discrepancy between the economic reality and the trend in the yen bond market," the official told Reuters.
The official added that an excessive concentration of funds in the yen bond market was one factor behind the slow recovery in Tokyo stocks.

Japan's economic recovery is becoming slightly firmer compared with the summer months, in line with some firming in consumption in addition to the production pick-up, another senior government official said.
The second official said he saw no need for implementing a supplementary budget, judging from the recovery trend.

A third government official said the market's outlook on the economy appeared to be too pessimistic, given that an economic outlook on Japan by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecast real growth of 2.7 percent for 1997.
He dismissed a notion that the government was becoming bullish on the economy only to avoid having to compile a supplementary budget, in view of the nation's budget woes.
